enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
1205 PM MDT Fri Oct 23 2026

...New DISCUSSION, AVIATION, FIRE WEATHER...

.KEY MESSAGES...
Updated at 1205 AM MDT Fri Oct 23 2026

 - A rare late-season risk of strong to severe thunderstorms will
   occur this evening. Widespread showers and thunderstorms
   developing across the South-Central New Mexico and Far West 
   Texas between 2 and 10 PM. Storms will be capable of large 
   hail, damaging winds, and localized flash flooding. 

 - More storm chances over the weekend, mostly east of the Rio
   Grande. Severe weather chances will also continue during this
   time. Highest local risks across Otero and Hudspeth Counties.

 - Drier weather expected early next week, but another round of
   rain chances looks likely after next Wednesday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1205 AM MDT Fri Oct 23 2026

Upper trough currently moving into the Great Basin region with
energy diving down the west side which will help cutoff a low
which will move into SW AZ by Sat morning. Do not see much
difference in the upper pattern across the CWA today into Sat. SSW
flow aloft with a pseudo dryline setup near the RGV will bring
scattered to widespread showers and thunderstorms late afternoon
and evening to eastern zones. Plenty of shear, mostly speed and
instability of around 500-1500J/kg CAPE. Current thinking is the 
tornado threat is minimal with higher LCL's and not much low level
backing. There will be a significant hail and wind threat into the
mid evening mainly RGV east. This setup will be nearly the same
for Saturday. It does look like a better chance for some multiple
rounds of thunderstorms Sat and there will be a higher chance for
flooding, but storms will still be moving quickly. May need a
Flood Watch, but will hold off for now. 

Heading into Sun/Mon, the upper low will slowly open up as it
moves across the central Rockies. This will keep a weak upper
trough lingering around the area and we keep some ESE surface
winds over southeastern CWA. NBM PoPs of slight chance near RGV to
likely east looks good. Could still see some severe storms these
days but shear will not be as impressive, but pretty good
instability remains. Temperatures will still remain about 5 
degrees above normal during this time. 

Another trough starts to approach the West Coast Wed-Thu and our
low level winds again to S to SE and tap some good moisture.
Chance PoPs return areawide by the end of the period. Temperatures
will continue to remain near to slightly above normal. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(18Z TAFS)
Issued at 1205 AM MDT Fri Oct 23 2026

P6SM SCT060-080 SCT-BKN120-150 to start the period. Isolated
storms over the higher terrain early on in the period will give
way to more widespread VRB20G35KT 1-3SM TSRAGR developing between
22Z-00Z and pushing NNE through the evening. All terminals could
see storms but KELP and KLRU most likely terminals to be affected
as well as areas to the NE. After 04Z, showers and TS will be
tapering off but some showers and isolated TS remain possible to
about 12Z. Lower clouds with some CIGS BKN020-030 possible,
especially on eastern mountain slopes. Winds generally S to SE AOB
12KTS except near thunderstorms. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1205 AM MDT Fri Oct 23 2026

Fire threats will remain low throughout the period with near
average temperatures and rain chances, especially eastern zones
almost daily. Temperatures will remain near to slightly above
normal with min RH's 25-30% southwest and 50-60% east. Winds will
not be an issue and will remain below 15mph except near
thunderstorms. Vent rates will be good to very good Sat and mainly
good on Sun.  

&&
